The main takeaway from our work is that
heparin, when administered to dogs in a dose of 100 IU per kilogram of body weight, does not cause any changes in the nitrogen metabolism of the myocardium under normal conditions.

heparin, administered intravenously at the initial stage, is capable of preventing the changes of nitrogen-containing biopolymer metabolism that develop under conditions of experimental myocardial infraction.

heparin, when used in the treatment of myocardial infarction, can be a valuable tool for the prevention of the development of some metabolic disorders in the injured tissue and for the activation of some metabolic processes.
